subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance / SLO requirements + regional routing (Finova)

Subject: Follow-up: Performance / SLO requirements + regional routing (Finova)

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery so we’re all aligned before the technical workshop: 

Recap of what we heard:
- Primary use case: customer-facing chat and light summarization for transaction flows (short prompts, frequent interactions).
- Expected peak: ~200 concurrent users initially, aiming to scale to ~2k concurrent users over 12 months.
- Typical prompt size: 50–120 tokens; average response length: 100–300 tokens.
- Strong requirement: EU data residency for EU customers (data must not leave EU for inference or logs).
- Multi-region expectation: route EU traffic to EU region; US traffic to US region; APAC is lower priority but expected in phase 2.

Performance/SLO items you asked to validate:
1) Latency targets: P95 end-to-end response latency target for chat (streaming enabled) — you suggested a ballpark of 200ms for the first tokens to begin streaming and ~600ms for tail for typical responses.
2) Throughput/concurrency: baseline for peak traffic (we heard target concurrent sessions ~200, growth to 2k).
3) Streaming: start-of-stream / first-byte latency and ability to deliver token-by-token streaming to web clients.
4) Regional routing & data residency: EU-only processing for EU customers; fallbacks should not violate residency.

Proposed next steps:
- Technical workshop with our SEs to validate realistic SLOs and run a targeted load test (I’ve looped in Aditya for scheduling).
- Share a short SLO/throughput matrix (attached) that outlines latency vs concurrency assumptions and options (hosted regional routing, dedicated capacity, private deployment).
- We’ll prepare a residency checklist for legal/IT to sign off (attached).

Questions for you before the workshop: 
- Can you confirm whether EU data residency requirement applies to model inputs only, or to outputs/logs/metrics as well?
- Do you have an initial example QPS or requests/sec estimate for peak? The concurrent users number helps but we’d like a rough requests/sec or messages/sec.
- Are you open to a short (30–60m) load-test window where Redwood runs synthetic traffic from EU and US regions to validate baseline numbers?

I’ll propose 2 slots for the workshop once you confirm the QPS estimate and residency boundaries.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

Residency scope:
- EU data residency must cover inputs, outputs, and any logs that contain PII or full request/response payloads. Aggregated metrics without PII can be stored outside EU.

Latency/throughput targets (initial phase):
- Non-streaming text-gen (standard completion): target P50 < 120ms, P95 < 400ms for 100-token responses at peak.
- Streaming chat: we care about time-to-first-token (TTFT) — target TTFT < 150ms, and sustained token streaming at least 20 tokens/sec for long responses.
- Peak concurrency: initial peak 200 concurrent chats, target scale to 2k concurrent within 12 months.
- QPS estimate: rough current peak is ~150 req/s (messages), planning for 800 req/s within quarter 2.

Other constraints:
- We will require TLS + customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest for EU-only data.
- Audit logs for EU tenants must be retained for 1 year within EU systems.

Yes to the load-test window — we can carve out a 1 hour slot. We’d like to run a focused session that validates TTFT and P95 at 200 concurrent users from EU and US endpoints.

Finally, can you confirm whether Redwood’s hosted offering can provide strict EU-only processing (no outbound logs) or whether we should plan for a Dedicated/Private deployment?

Alex

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance / SLO requirements + regional routing (Finova)

Alex / team — quick technical notes and options ahead of the workshop. Thanks for the detail — very helpful.

How Redwood can meet the requirements (short answers):
- EU residency: Hosted API in EU region can be configured to keep inference and logs in-region; for strict contractual guarantees (no egress of any data), Dedicated or Private deployment with customer-managed KMS is the stronger path. We can scope both in the workshop.
- Latency: P50/P95 targets depend on model choice and sequence length. For short prompts (50–120 tokens) we can hit P50 < 100–150ms and P95 in the 200–500ms range on optimized models (fp16/quantized) with continuous batching tuned for low-latency workloads.
- Streaming TTFT: we have a streaming path optimized for sub-150ms TTFT for small prompt sizes when requests are routed to nearest region with warm KV cache. First-byte latency is most sensitive to model cold starts and KV cache misses.
- Throughput/concurrency: sustained 200 concurrent chat sessions is a routine scenario on hosted with regional routing; scaling to 2k concurrent will likely require Dedicated capacity or autoscaling policies with predictable warm pools to avoid cold-start tail latency.

Technical clarifications we’d like before the workshop:
1) Target model family / quality bar (open models vs proprietary) — which fidelity do you expect? Higher-fidelity models increase latency/cost.
2) Typical prompt->response token distribution at peak (helps size batching).
3) Are there strict egress restrictions for logs/metrics or is anonymized metrics acceptable?

Attached is a simple SLO vs concurrency matrix (redwood-slo-matrix.pdf) that maps expected P95 at different concurrency buckets and deployment options. During the workshop we can run a 1-hour load test that measures TTFT, P95, and tokens/sec with synthetic traffic and your sample prompts.

Proposed workshop agenda (30–60m):
- 10m: confirm residency and security checklist (legal/IT can join)
- 15m: run a short smoke test from EU and US regions (Aditya to lead)
- 10–20m: review results and next steps (Dedicated sizing / Private proposal if needed)

I’ll propose two slots in the next note — please confirm availability.

— Aditya
